santizeAnchors in VerifyMessageProperties.java pairs anchor tags strictly positionally (i-th anchor in translation must string-equal i-th anchor in English), falsely rejecting legitimate translations that reorder two links or drop an earlier link while keeping a later one, contradicting the javadoc's stated set-membership intent

santizeAnchors on anchor mismatch breaks the loop but returns value with the offending anchor still present, so the subsequent sanitizer pass strips it and emits a redundant second 'Illegal HTML' finding for the same root cause; the anchor error message also omits key/file context unlike the other message

verifySafeHtml throws I/O failures (including the derived English path not existing, produced by blind replaceAll string surgery on the absolute path: resources-community→resources plus locale-suffix regex) as a raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException, aborting the whole verification with a stack trace rather than an actionable per-file report

ANCHOR_PATTERN '</?a[^>]*>' also matches <abbr>, <area>, <article>, <aside>, <address>, etc.; such tags appearing in both English and a translation are silently stripped as 'anchors' before sanitization, letting non-allow-listed elements pass the check, or otherwise produce a misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' error; pattern should require a word boundary (e.g. '</?a[\s>]')

verifySafeHtml re-opens and re-parses the English properties bundle from disk for every processed locale file and reads the target file a second time (already read via Files.readString in verify()); with ~60 locales per message bundle this is substantial redundant I/O - the English bundle should be parsed once (e.g. cached per directory) and the already-read contents reused

All new tests in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest are negative cases; there is no positive test asserting that a valid translation (allowed p/br/b/strong tags, correctly matching anchors, the {2,choice,...} pattern in error-invalid-multivalued-size, templateHelp's CLAIM.<NAME>, optimizeLookupHelp's <Extensions>, email RTL style stripping) produces zero findings, so regressions in the key-specific normalizeValue workarounds or accidental over-strictness would not be caught

adjudication_records.issue_text: santizeAnchors in VerifyMessageProperties.java pairs anchor tags strictly positionally (i-th anchor in translation must string-equal i-th anchor in English), falsely rejecting legitimate translations that reorder two links or drop an earlier link while keeping a later one, contradicting the javadoc's stated set-membership intent

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, anchors are validated by iterating translation anchors with `matcher.find()` while simultaneously advancing `englishMatcher.find()` and requiring `Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`. This enforces strict positional/sequence equality of anchor tags between translation and English. The Javadoc says “Allow only those anchor tags from the source key to also appear in the target key”, which implies set/subset membership, not ordered 1:1 pairing. As written, legitimate translations that reorder links or omit an earlier link but keep a later one will be flagged with “Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string”, i.e., a false positive introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: santizeAnchors on anchor mismatch breaks the loop but returns value with the offending anchor still present, so the subsequent sanitizer pass strips it and emits a redundant second 'Illegal HTML' finding for the same root cause; the anchor error message also omits key/file context unlike the other message

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(...)`, on a mismatch it `break`s without removing the offending `<a...>` tag(s) from `value`, then `verifySafeHtml()` continues to sanitize that same `value` with a policy that does not allow `<a>` (POLICY_SOME_HTML only allows `br,p,strong,b`). This will typically cause an additional `"Illegal HTML in key ..."` message after the earlier `"Didn't find anchor tag ..."`, i.e., potentially redundant reporting for the same underlying issue. Also, the anchor-mismatch message (`messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")`) lacks key/file context unlike the Illegal HTML message which includes `key` and `file`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml throws I/O failures (including the derived English path not existing, produced by blind replaceAll string surgery on the absolute path: resources-community→resources plus locale-suffix regex) as a raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException, aborting the whole verification with a stack trace rather than an actionable per-file report

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), verifySafeHtml() is called inside the try block that only catches IOException from Files.readString/verifyNoDuplicateKeys, but verifySafeHtml() itself catches IOExceptions (both for `file` and for the derived `englishFile`) and rethrows them as raw RuntimeException (`throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file ...", e);`). The derived English path is computed via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`, so if that path does not exist or the regex replacement produces a wrong filename, the plugin will throw RuntimeException and abort verification rather than returning an actionable per-file message list / MojoExecutionException.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ANCHOR_PATTERN '</?a[^>]*>' also matches <abbr>, <area>, <article>, <aside>, <address>, etc.; such tags appearing in both English and a translation are silently stripped as 'anchors' before sanitization, letting non-allow-listed elements pass the check, or otherwise produce a misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' error; pattern should require a word boundary (e.g. '</?a[\s>]')

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties, `ANCHOR_PATTERN` is `Pattern.compile("]*>")`, which matches any tag starting with the letter `a` (e.g., ``, `
`, etc.), not just ``/``. In `santizeAnchors()`, any such matched tag that also appears (identically) in the English source is stripped from the translation *before* running the OWASP sanitizer, so disallowed elements can be removed silently and therefore evade the intended “Illegal HTML” detection. If such tags don’t match the English tag sequence, the code emits the misleading message “Didn't find anchor tag ...” for non-anchor tags. This behavior is directly verifiable from the regex and the pre-sanitization stripping logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml re-opens and re-parses the English properties bundle from disk for every processed locale file and reads the target file a second time (already read via Files.readString in verify()); with ~60 locales per message bundle this is substantial redundant I/O - the English bundle should be parsed once (e.g. cached per directory) and the already-read contents reused

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows redundant file I/O/parsing: verify() already reads the target properties file via Files.readString(file.toPath()), but verifySafeHtml() re-reads the same file again using new FileInputStream(file) to build a PropertyResourceBundle. It also computes an englishFile path and opens/parses that English bundle inside verifySafeHtml() for every processed locale file (i.e., per VerifyMessageProperties invocation). This is a real efficiency/architecture concern grounded in the added code, but it does not constitute a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All new tests in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest are negative cases; there is no positive test asserting that a valid translation (allowed p/br/b/strong tags, correctly matching anchors, the {2,choice,...} pattern in error-invalid-multivalued-size, templateHelp's CLAIM.<NAME>, optimizeLookupHelp's <Extensions>, email RTL style stripping) produces zero findings, so regressions in the key-specific normalizeValue workarounds or accidental over-strictness would not be caught

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds substantial new validation logic in VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), including key-specific normalization exceptions in normalizeValue() (templateHelp CLAIM.<NAME>, optimizeLookupHelp <Extensions>, choice-pattern stripping for error-invalid-multivalued-size/linkExpirationFormatter.*, and email RTL style removal) plus anchor handling in santizeAnchors(). However, the newly added tests in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest only assert failure/negative cases (illegalHtmlTag_en.properties, noHtml_de.properties, changedAnchor_de.properties) and the existing duplicate-key test remains a negative case. There is no test asserting that a valid properties file with allowed tags (br/p/b/strong), matching anchors, and the normalizeValue() workarounds yields an empty findings list, so over-strictness or regressions in those exceptions would not be caught.
